questions.question: What are the data types and variables in Ruby?
questions.title: Data Types and Variables in Ruby
questions.direct_answer: Ruby is dynamically typed (a variable's type is its current value; you don't declare types). Core types: Numbers (Integer 42, Float 3.14), Strings ('single' or "double" — double interpolates #{...}), Symbols (:name — immutable, interned strings, good for keys), Booleans (true, false), nil (no value), Arrays ([1,2]), Hashes ({k:v}), Ranges (1..5). Variables: local (x), instance (@x), class (@@x), global ($x), constant (UPPER). Everything is an object — even numbers: 42.times{}, 3.14.round, nil.nil?. Assignment is by reference for objects; variables are just labels pointing to objects. Use .class to check a type, and duck typing: if it walks like a duck, call walk — don't check the type.

interviewer_intent.testing: Whether you know Ruby is dynamically typed, the core types (Integer/String/Symbol/Array/Hash/nil), and the variable scopes (local/instance/class/global/constant).
interviewer_intent.common_mistake: Checking types with == (use .class or duck typing), or confusing symbol (:a) and string ('a') keys.
interviewer_intent.to_stand_out: Ruby is dynamically typed. Types: Integer, Float, String, Symbol, Array, Hash, Range, Boolean, nil. Vars: local x, @x instance, @@x class, $x global, UPPER const. Everything is an object.

sections.title: Data types and variables
sections.content:
```ruby
# Dynamic typing (no type declarations):
x = 42        # Integer
x = 'hi'      # now a String (type = current value)
x.class       # String  (check a type with .class)

# Core types:
42            # Integer
3.14          # Float
' single '     # String (no interpolation)
"#{1+1}"       # String (interpolated -> '2')
:name          # Symbol (immutable, interned; great for hash keys)
true, false    # Booleans
nil            # no value (nil.nil? == true)
[1, 2, 3]      # Array
{ k: 'v' }     # Hash
(1..5)         # Range

# Variable scopes:
local_var = 1        # local
class Box
  @@count = 0         # class variable
  CONST = 10           # constant (UPPER; can be reassigned with warning)
  def initialize; @x = 0; end   # @x: instance variable
end
$global = 1          # global (avoid; use sparingly)

# EVERYTHING is an object:
42.times { |i| puts i }    # even integers have methods
nil.nil?                   # true
3.14.round(1)              # 3.1

# Duck typing: don't check the type; call the method.
#   def speak(x); x.sound; end   # works for Dog, Cat, anything with .sound
```
